extracted.intended_audience: Advanced high school, undergraduate, and graduate students in technical fields; professional mathematicians, physicists, engineers, chemists, biologists, and computer scientists.
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and communicating mathematics professionally, covering grammar and style, mathematical exposition (theorems, proofs, definitions), publishing procedures, letters and reports, books, and modern electronic tools (TeX, email, graphics). Intended as a primer for those working in the mathematical profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syntax, grammar, structure, and style
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a primary topic the book addresses; general rules and prescriptions about grammatical and stylistic correctness for mathematical prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical exposition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad guidance on how to write expository mathematical material (treatment described elsewhere in Table of Contents under Chapter 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the computer and TeX
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of the computer and TeX
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats practical aspects of preparing documents electronically and the role of TeX in mathematical typesetting (expanded in Chapter 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: E-mail etiquette
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice on professional email communication in the mathematical community (also appears under Chapter 4 and 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: All aspects of publishing a journal article
rubrics_metrics.description: All aspects of publishing a journal article
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers procedural and quality aspects of preparing and submitting journal manuscripts; one of the book's central practical topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing persuasive grant proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: How to write grant proposals that are persuasive and compelling
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book outlines strategies for proposal-writing aimed to persuade reviewers and funding bodies (mentioned in the synopsis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of recommendation content
rubrics_metrics.description: How to write a letter of recommendation describing the research abilities of a candidate for promotion or tenure; what a dean is looking for in a letter
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on tone, content, and expectations for recommendation letters for academic advancement (listed among practical topics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Book proposal writing
rubrics_metrics.description: How to write a book proposal to a publisher
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical advice for preparing a book proposal aimed at publishers (noted in introductory description and Chapter 5 topics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applying for a job / job materials
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice on job application materials and strategies; cross-referenced with 'Your Vita, Your Grant, Your Job, Your Life' in Chapter 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who Is My Audience?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes identifying and writing for the correct readership; listed as a basic topic in Chapter 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing and Thought

rubrics_metrics.name: Say What You Mean; Mean What You Say
rubrics_metrics.description: Say What You Mean; Mean What You Say

rubrics_metrics.name: Compound sentences; passive voice
